items.title: feat(android): unified rooted device control, local + outbound remote mode
items.body:
## Goal

Provide one privileged Android device-control core inside Alice Pro with both local loopback and outbound remote modes. No Termux fork and no second root agent.

## Root core
One foreground RootAgentService owns bounded su-based shell/screenshot/UI/tap/swipe/text/key/package/process operations with explicit lifecycle and timeout/cancellation cleanup. Screenshot success requires a valid complete image.

## Local mode
Privileged API binds only to 127.0.0.1. Credentials use Keystore-backed protection. WebView/native privileged bridges are origin-scoped and external navigation cannot inherit access.

## Outbound mode
The phone initiates the connection to Alice for NAT-safe remote control. Pairing binds device to authenticated owner; queue/result/replay are idempotent and bounded; one device cannot claim another's commands.

## Tool boundary
Read-only inspection may be permitted by policy; shell/input/open-url are privileged actions and retain normal approval. Trace contains sanitized bounded metadata only.

## Acceptance
Local + outbound modes share the same root core; owner/device isolation, malformed/oversized/replay/timeout cases fail closed; restart recovers; real-device tests prove root/WebView behavior not demonstrable in unit tests.

Supersedes #648 and absorbs #683.

## Remote job/result transport

Outbound/local device execution must preserve bounded job/result correlation (job/agent/trace/invocation identity), sanitized failures, timeout/cancellation and replay/idempotency semantics. Persistence uses canonical #776 rather than SQL tables. Historical protocol/reference implementation: PR #656.

Android Keystore is the Android backend of canonical Secret Store #755; RootAgent pairing/auth secrets are resolved through that boundary and are not duplicated into #776 or app logs/Trace.

## Minimal first slice

Prove one local RootAgentService core before remote mode:
- foreground lifecycle;
- loopback-only privileged API;
- bounded read-only device info + one harmless shell probe;
- timeout/cancellation;
- Android Keystore/#755 pairing credential primitive;
- origin isolation;
- real-device smoke.

Do not implement outbound remote queue or broad input/package/process mutation until the local root boundary is proven.

## Current-master result-bridge verification — 2026-10-05

Fresh repository search confirms the historical #656 local-agent result bridge is not already present on current protected master:

- `local_agents/results.py` is absent;
- the focused result-retrieval tests from #656 are absent.

Treat #656 as historical protocol/source material only. Any outbound/local device job-result transport must be rebuilt against #776 and the current RootAgent/tool boundaries.


## Incremental acceptance policy

Local RootAgent core, result transport and outbound remote mode may merge as separate verified slices. After each merge, mark the proven device boundary shipped and leave only the missing remote/control capabilities. Do not broaden privileges merely to make one PR appear complete.


## Redmi 9 Live Server connectivity repair — 2026-10-11
Refs #1161 and draft PR #1162. The **existing loopback Live Server** on Redmi 9 was repaired (not the new privileged RootAgent core): HTTP 503 came from ADB's two connected devices while the legacy adapter required exactly one. The service is now pinned fail-closed to `Redmi_9/galahad` from a private on-device policy. The prior hard-coded Mobile Legends foreground restriction was removed without removing Bearer auth, loopback isolation or bounded verbs. Authorized `wake` was added; unauthorized requests still return HTTP 401, unknown action returns 400.

Verified on the primary service: `/health`, `/status`, `/screen/semantics`, `/screen/tree` and `/screen/capture` return HTTP **200**; `wake` returns 200 **submitted, not evidence of unlocking**. 7 local unit regressions PASS; Redmi 9 was selected even with another phone connected; primary PID 16899; independent RDC never restarted. Backups and regression scripts are private on the phone, not yet committed.

This is a **staging connectivity fix only**, not approval of the root privilege boundary, keyboard, clipboard, physical Android InputReader E2E or merge. Canonical tracked source migration, exact-head CI, real Live Server controller/session issuance and user acceptance remain outstanding. No unrelated stream actions.


## Review: Live Server Redmi 9 hardening — 2026-10-11

**Scope:** review of already-running private Redmi 9 `~/.alice-rdc/android_live_server.py`, `android_actions.py`, `android_accessibility.py`, `android_screen_dom.py`, `android_state_merge.py`, `android_state_store.py` after removing hard-coded Mobile Legends allowlist. **No live mutations, restart or merge during this review.** On-device private sources are not in PR #1162.

### VERIFIED — working boundary
- Primary Live Server remains available at loopback `127.0.0.1:8765`; authenticated `/health` and `/status` HTTP 200, anonymous `/status` and `/screen/dom` HTTP 401. Unknown `key_down` and `clipboard_set` commands HTTP 400 (not implemented, not proof that keyboard/clipboard work).
- Existing unit suite **7/7 PASS** after repair; prior smoke reported `/screen/tree`, semantics and capture HTTP 200 on non-Mobile-Legends focus.
- `android_public_tree.py` really strips source text/identifiers; no evidence of arbitrary shell command accepted.

### P1-01 — device identity is metadata-only (reproduced with mock)
`android_actions.py:device()` selects any *already ADB-authorized* device with `model=Redmi_9` and `device=galahad`. In synthetic ADB fixture with only a substituted transport (same fields, different serial), selector accepted it. Real-device wrong-target execution is **NOT** claimed. Add pairing-bound owner/device identity and check the same device identity before dispatch, not just public model/device metadata. Reject disconnect/replace/reconnect races.

### P1-02 — OCR and snapshot are not redacted like screen/tree (source + synthetic repro)
`/screen/dom` returns `diff`, `state` and `layout` built from raw `node["text"]` in `android_screen_dom.py` and `android_state_merge.py`. `StateStore.save` stores these nodes in the private local checkpoint. Synthetic `SYNTHETIC_PRIVATE_MARKER` appears in state nodes/events (confirmed) while `public_tree` redacts it. On authorized sensitive screens this may expose PIN prompts, notifications or financial/account information. **Not an unauthenticated API leak** (Bearer 401 confirmed); it is a missing per-surface privacy/retention policy. `android_accessibility.py` also writes a UI hierarchy to fixed `/sdcard/alice-ui.xml` without cleanup. Require explicit policy for private apps/lockscreen, redacted outputs, short storage TTL and bounded cleanup.

### P1-03 — lockscreen scope is not separated (synthetic guard repro)
`safe_screen()` only checks trusted model result and that `focus` is a string. When a mocked focus was `com.android.systemui/.keyguard.KeyguardView`, it returned **True**. Thus any bearer-authenticated controller gets the same generic screen/click functionality at lockscreen as in normal apps. Intended owner-approved unlock may remain possible, but introduce a separate lockscreen permission/mode and no unrestricted credential entry or repeated PIN attempts. No actual PIN or lockscreen interaction was attempted in review.

### P2-04 — action acknowledgments are not acceptance
`/action` uses `submitted: true, verified: false` from the ADB adapter; HTTP 200 does not confirm foreground effect, button release, unlock or clipboard. Add command/result IDs, postcondition, bounded trace, explicit states submitted/observed/verified, timeout and teardown tests.

### P2-05 — concurrency/recovery issues to test
`safe_screen` and `/status` change process-wide `os.environ["ANDROID_SERIAL"]` in a threaded HTTP server; `android_accessibility.py` runs unqualified `adb shell`. Prefer explicit `-s` on every subprocess, not mutable global environment. Promotion rollback restores the old adapter which was already known to return 503 with two phones; `check_ready(strict=False)` still requires `/status == 200`. Fault-inject startup/port contention and prove independent recovery.

### P1-06 — implementation is not yet versioned / Live Server input not completed
Repair exists **only** under private `~/.alice-rdc/` files and backups; not tracked by canonical repository PR and not independently CI-gated. PR [#1162](https://github.com/maksimp6/Chat/pull/1162) is green for **synthetic** stage but does not include deployed Live Server adapter. GET `/health` advertises only `back, home, open, screenshot, status, swipe, tap, wake`; real signed mouse/keyboard/clipboard, root C verifier and Unicode IME are still absent.

**Disposition:** FAIL REVIEW for release/merge readiness; keep live service running and RDC recovery intact. Do not equate CI GREEN, request accepted or screen captured with end-to-end user acceptance. Next: isolate confidential UI policy, cryptographic target identity, per-call ADB binding, version-controlled Live Server service + RED→GREEN tests, then real Live Server-only E2E and user acceptance. Do not touch unrelated Dota/Xtra user streams. **NO MERGE.**


## P1 remediation deployed and CI-verified (2026-10-11)

**Scope:** only actual Redmi 9 Live Server on localhost `127.0.0.1:8765`. No Dota/Xtra stream involvement. No RDC self-restart, no merge.

- **P1 target identity hardening:** pin exact enrolled authorized ADB serial + `model=Redmi_9`/`device=galahad` + verified 16-hex Android secure ID, fail closed on missing/changed transport/ID. This is still **not cryptographic device attestation** and should be supplanted by #650 signed/verifier root boundary.
- **P1 lockscreen:** parse Android `isKeyguardShowing` fail closed. HTTP endpoint *and* final ADB action adapter deny touch/app launch on Keyguard. Only safe `wake` remains possible without PIN entry. `/status` hides focus/serial. `POST /action status` now 400 (privacy-bypass closed).
- **P1 OCR surface:** `/screen/dom` returns redacted geometrical tree and no raw `diff/state/layout`; no automatic raw OCR StateStore restore/save. Legacy local checkpoint/journal generated by the service purged after successful deployment. Accessibility now uses per-call `adb -s` and a private `/data/local/tmp` XML with finally cleanup instead of permanent shared `/sdcard/alice-ui.xml` writes.
- **Runtime evidence** from primary process **PID 19175**: authenticated health/status HTTP 200; anonymous requests 401; `POST /action tap` and `open` rejected HTTP 423 while phone locked; `/screen/tree` 403; `/screen/dom` 423; `POST /action status` 400. Isolated candidate HTTP smoke and 17 local unit tests PASS.
- Local backup saved before atomic swap; RDC unmodified. No secrets, PIN, actual serial, raw UI XML or screenshots published.
- New version-controlled **draft [PR #1163](https://github.com/maksimp6/Chat/pull/1163)** at head `6fc2b8e563e06b38466e9b553e7cc50f5f844121`: [CI 38175444824](https://github.com/maksimp6/Chat/actions/runs/38175444824) SUCCESS, Python **2,686 passed, 8 skipped**; CodeQL/Security/Format/Dependency review/Local smoke SUCCESS.
- **Still not complete:** legacy `/sdcard/alice-ui.xml` leftover from prior versions not explicitly verified purged; full crypto owner/session verification and cross-process root isolation, real uinput/clipboard/IME E2E, crash-recovery orphans and owner acceptance unverified. No phone unlocking performed. **NO MERGE**.

items.title: fix(desktop): send Windows system DNS through the tun with an xray core
items.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #261 (row 9 of the leftovers audit). #261 stopped routing the system resolvers past the tun, but on Windows a resolver on the LAN (usually the router) was still asked directly: its on-link route is more specific than the `0/1` + `128/1` split-default, and `apply_external_tun_routing` ignored its `_capture_dns` argument. Linux solved this with a port-53 policy rule. Windows has no port-based routing, so this PR points the DNS client at the tun and closes port 53 everywhere else for as long as the helper runs.

When the data-path is xray behind an external tun with the uplink bind (the same `capture_dns` condition as on Linux), bring-up now:

- gives the wintun adapter `198.18.0.2` as its only DNS server. That address is the new `kasumi_core::tun::TUN_DNS_IPV4`, inside the tun's on-link `/15`, so a query to it enters the tun, where #261's `hijack_inbound_dns` answers it from the core's DNS module. The call is [`SetInterfaceDnsSettings`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/netioapi/nf-netioapi-setinterfacednssettings) (Windows 10 2004+), resolved with `GetProcAddress` at run time so older builds still load the app; without it, `netsh interface ipv4 set dnsservers … validate=no` is used;
- sets the tun's interface metric to 1, so Windows lists and asks the tun first ([interface metric](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/network-subsystem/net-sub-interface-metric));
- opens a **dynamic** WFP session (`FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC`) and adds, in one transaction, a max-weight sublayer with these filters at `ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4`/`V6`: permit the core's executable (app id of `xray.exe`, weight 15), permit anything on the tun's LUID (14), permit UDP/TCP 53 to `198.18.0.2` (13, v4), block UDP/TCP 53 (12). Without the block, Windows 8.1+ also sends each query in parallel to every other adapter's servers, so the LAN resolver would still answer. The core stays permitted because it resolves its own upstreams (e.g. a `direct` resolver) out of the uplink.

The filter set mirrors two upstream implementations: sing-tun's `strict_route` in `tun_windows.go` (dynamic session, `MaxUint16` sublayer, own-process permit above a tun-interface permit above a port-53 block, connect layers only) and wireguard-windows' `tunnel/firewall` (`blockDNS` with UDP/TCP protocol conditions and permitted DNS servers, `permitTunInterface` by LUID via `FWPM_CONDITION_IP_LOCAL_INTERFACE`, everything inside one `FwpmTransaction`). All verdicts are soft (no `CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT`), so they only settle our sublayer and leave other firewalls' blocks in force.

**Crash behaviour.** Nothing here outlives the helper. The adapter DNS and metric live on the wintun adapter and go with it. The WFP filters belong to the helper's engine handle: the base filtering engine deletes a dynamic session's objects when that handle closes, and the kernel closes it when the process exits for any reason, `TerminateProcess` included. So if the helper crashes or is killed, the filters vanish and DNS falls back to the normal resolvers: a possible DNS leak until Kasumi is started again, never a machine without DNS. A normal stop drops the guard first in `clear_external_tun_routing`. Nothing is written to the registry or the route state for DNS, so there is nothing to recover at the next start or on `--uninstall`.

sing-box is unchanged. A native sing-box tun already gets the same kind of dynamic WFP DNS block from sing-tun when the user turns on `strict_route`, so it isn't doubled here. A socks-only sing-box behind an external tun resolves server names through the system resolvers itself, so `capture_dns` stays off for it, as on Linux.

The bindings come from `windows-sys` 0.59, which `src-tauri` already uses directly: only the `Win32_NetworkManagement_WindowsFilteringPlatform`, `Win32_System_Rpc`, `Win32_NetworkManagement_{IpHelper,Ndis}` and `Win32_System_LibraryLoader` features are added, with no new crate and no `Cargo.lock` change. The plan (which filters, which conditions, which weights) is plain data in `desktop/windows/dns_guard.rs`; the apply layer only converts it to `FWPM_*` structs and calls WFP.

CI's `desktop-windows` job now also runs `cargo test -p kasumi-desktop --lib -- desktop::windows::`.

## Affected layer

- [ ] `frontend/` — React Web UI
- [x] `crates/` · `src-tauri/` — Rust core / backend / Tauri desktop
- [ ] `module/` — Android installable zip (thin launcher over the Rust daemon)
- [ ] `scripts/` — build / release helpers
- [x] CI / `.github/`
- [ ] Docs only

## Verification

Rust (`crates/` · `src-tauri/`):

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` (603 passed); new `tun_dns_is_on_link_but_not_the_tun_itself` in kasumi-core
- [x] Codegen drift: `cargo run -p kasumi-desktop --example codegen` leaves `git` clean

Web UI (`frontend/`): not touched.

- [ ] `bun run check` — Biome lint + format clean
- [ ] `bun run test` — vitest green
- [ ] `bun run build` — `tsc -b` + vite build succeed
- [ ] `bun run check:i18n` — locale dictionaries in sync (if any user-visible string changed)

Module shell (`module/`): not touched.

- [ ] `shellcheck -s sh module/*.sh`

Windows, cross-built from Linux (`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, rust 1.95.0 + mingw-w64):

- [x] `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --workspace --exclude kasumi-daemon --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, on every commit.
- [x] Under Wine 11 all 11 `desktop::windows::` tests pass. The DNS guard is covered as data: `plan_blocks_dns_outside_the_tun_only` (only UDP/TCP 53 is ever blocked, and the tun, the core and the tun resolver are permitted above it on both families), `guard_is_dynamic_and_persists_nothing` (session flag is exactly `FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC`; no sublayer or filter carries `PERSISTENT`/`BOOTTIME`), `raw_conditions_carry_their_values`, and `route_state_records_only_routes` (the route state has no DNS record to replay). `adapter_dns_fails_cleanly_for_a_missing_interface` also shows the binary still loads and falls back when `SetInterfaceDnsSettings` is missing (Wine's `iphlpapi.dll` lacks it).
- [x] `closing_the_engine_removes_the_guard` installs the real plan (with every block turned into a permit, so nothing is filtered) into the base filtering engine, checks the sublayer exists from a second session, drops the guard and checks it is gone. Wine has no filtering engine (`RPC_S_CANNOT_SUPPORT`), so there it is skipped; on the elevated GitHub Windows runner it runs for real. Without admin rights it is skipped too.

## Checklist

- [x] Title is a scoped Conventional Commit; commits are logically split
- [x] No build artifacts committed (`module/bin/<abi>/`, `geoip`/`geosite`, built `module/webroot/`, `src-tauri/gen/` — all gitignored on purpose)
- [x] Generated `frontend/src/generated/` was regenerated from Rust, not hand-edited
- [ ] If user-visible strings changed: `i18n/en.ts` **and every** locale file updated (no partial translations)
- [ ] Renames touching the project id were grepped in all case forms (`kasumi-proxy`, `Kasumi Proxy`, camelCase)

## Notes for reviewers

- **Nothing here was run on real Windows.** It needs a Windows 10/11 box with wintun, xray + tun2socks and a LAN resolver. Checks to do there:
  - while connected, `netsh wfp show filters` lists the "Kasumi Proxy DNS guard" sublayer's filters, and `Get-DnsClientServerAddress` / `Get-NetIPInterface` show `198.18.0.2` and metric 1 on the wintun adapter;
  - `Resolve-DnsName` works, a packet capture on the LAN adapter shows no port-53 traffic to the router, and xray's log shows `[socks-in -> dns-out]`;
  - a routing rule that sends a domain to a plain `direct` resolver still resolves (the `xray.exe` app-id permit);
  - after Stop, and after `taskkill /F` of the helper or service, the filters are gone and DNS works without Kasumi running;
  - the `netsh` fallback on a pre-2004 build;
  - the CI run of `closing_the_engine_removes_the_guard` actually installs (not skips) on the runner.
- The block covers every port-53 connect outside the tun, loopback included, as wireguard-windows does. A local DNS proxy on `127.0.0.1:53` is unreachable while connected. DoH/DoT (443/853) are not touched.
- Machines with domain or corporate DNS: while connected, every name, internal ones included, goes to the core's DNS module. That is what "DNS via proxy" asks for, but it differs from today's leaky behaviour. There is no opt-out for domain-joined machines yet.
- If the guard can't be installed (no BFE, an older build rejecting a condition), bring-up logs a warning and continues with the adapter DNS and metric only, i.e. today's partial behaviour.
- This conflicts textually with the job-object PR (#326) in the `desktop-windows` CI steps (both append a test step; keep both) and with the multi-session PR (#328) in `ci.yml` and `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`. Whichever merges later needs a small rebase.

```
Missing DLL: api-ms-win-core-psapi-ansi-l1-1-0.dll  Function: K32GetModuleBaseNameA
```

## Symptoms <!-- What's the problem? -->
Origin client installs, after install when it attempts to launch the game it shows the following error "There is a problem with your game's setup. Please reinstall your game." afterwards nothing happens.

2. Let Steam install deps and wait for Origin client install to appear
3. Follow on-screen instructions to complete Origin client install
4. Wait for the error to show after the Origin client has launched and it attempts to start the game

## Intent

Earlier: make sure to use the browser and test everything, click and see user journey, the buttons, the features; once I am back we will focus on design and fix the user journey and experience. The remaining things are the signed-in QA findings: venue photo wall publish and owner remove; nav Sign in popover covered by the profile header and opening by itself after sign-out; Welcome back greeting and user_signed_in firing on every page load; the 18+ confirmation door for Wanted, Diary and Step Out (under-18 date of birth must not block sign-up); Save to a list chip saved state; Step Out web push offered in browsers that support it; Wanted and Diary rows editable, removable and the saved link clickable; Pub Pal setup asking 18+ once, landing at the top, and consistent voice wording. > [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Broad touch on auth session events, age-gate reads/writes, and new owner edit/delete APIs; behavior is heavily tested but complexity grew in Pal setup and save-list race handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR tightens **signed-in account journeys** across auth, contribution gating, private lists, saves, Step Out, Pub Pal, and venue photos—mostly UX and API behavior, with owner-scoped edit/delete where lists were read-only before.
> 
> **Contribution “we ask once.”** Reads of your own Wanted, Diary, Step Out, and cheap-pint settings now return **HTTP 200 with gate status** (`adult_check_required`, handle onboarding, etc.) instead of 409s that looked like load failures. **`ContributionGateDoor`** replaces those errors with inline copy and a single **“I’m 18 or over”** tap; one assertion is broadcast so every door on the page clears and lists refetch. Writes still refuse with 409. Pub Pal **`GET /api/pub-pal`** adds **`adultOnFile`** so setup can skip the redundant 18+ step when the account already answered.
> 
> **Diary and Wanted ownership.** Diary gains **`update` / `delete`** on `POST /api/diary` plus profile UI to edit day, rating, review, or remove entries. Wanted adds **`note`** edits, safe **http/https “Open saved link”** helpers, and row controls (edit note, remove, fulfilled rows remove-only).
> 
> **Save to a list.** Chips show **`aria-pressed`**, save/remove toasts, waits for server membership before enabling writes, and resets state on account or venue switches so stale presses don’t lie.
> 
> **Auth and nav.** Session **restore** no longer fires welcome / **`user_signed_in`** analytics; the session transition tracker ignores boot-order **`SIGNED_IN`** before **`INITIAL_SESSION`**. **Sign out** closes the account menu so the sign-in popover doesn’t open alone. Wanted “Save for a night” uses the viewer session seam for sign-in vs unresolved session.
> 
> **Step Out web push** only nags iPhone/iPad browser tabs to add to Home Screen; desktop and Android tabs can register push in-browser, with clearer blocked/unsupported copy and native-app messaging.
> 
> **Venue photos:** crop with **Use photo** does not publish; **Post photo** submits; owners get **Remove** on the wall (with account-switch-safe refetch).
> 
> Smaller fixes: analytics consent no longer scrolls under a hidden card; web push allows vetted Windows endpoints; README and gate copy point at shared contribution access rules; history-wait helpers de-flake wizard tests.
